paraphrase: The Kāśī Khaṇḍa's teaching that Kāśī is the liberating city: those who die there are liberated by Śiva, who at the moment of death imparts the saving (tāraka) instruction.
speaker: Skanda (frame)

paraphrase: Agastya to Lopāmudrā on the inner (mānasa) tīrthas: truth, forbearance, sense-control, compassion for all beings, straightforwardness, giving, self-restraint, contentment, celibacy, kind speech, knowledge, steadiness and austerity are tīrthas, and the supreme tīrtha is the purity of the mind; bathing the body in water is not bathing - the greedy, cruel and hypocritical remain impure after bathing in every tīrtha, as fish born and dying in water do not reach heaven; where one who has mastered the senses lives, there are Kurukṣetra, Naimiṣa and Puṣkara; the earthly tīrthas are holy through the power of earth and water and the presence of sages, so one should resort to both.

paraphrase: At Prabhāsa the liṅga Pāśupateśvara is the abode of the Pāśupatas; there the Pāśupata siddhas, brahmins devoted to celibacy, calm and self-controlled, reached supreme perfection and went to Śiva's abode in this very body; the chapter cites the ash formula 'fire is ash, wind is ash'.
